title: Must / Have To
objectives: Use must / have to accurately in A2 contexts.
Understand form, meaning, and typical usage.
Produce short spoken and written examples.
canDo: I can express obligation with must and have to.

warmUp.title: Activate prior knowledge
warmUp.prompt: Before this lesson, recall what you know about must / have to. How is it similar or different from Portuguese?
reflectionQuestions: When do native speakers use must / have to?
Can you think of one example?

explanation:
Must = speaker obligation/rules | Have to = external rules

Mustn't = prohibition | Don't have to = no obligation

grammar.title: Must / Have To
grammar.rule: Must = speaker obligation/rules | Have to = external rules

reading.title: Must / Have To in Context
reading.text: Employees must badge in. I have to catch the 7 a.m. train. You don't have to bring food — lunch is included. You mustn't use your phone in the exam.

questions.question: What is the main topic of the text?
questions.explanation: The text illustrates this lesson topic.

questions.question: Is this text appropriate for A2 learners?
Which sentence best matches the lesson?

writing.prompt: Write a short paragraph (5–7 sentences) using must / have to. Use at least 3 words from the vocabulary list.
rubricHints: Use the target structure at least twice.
writing.modelAnswer: You must wear a seatbelt. I have to finish today. You mustn't smoke here. You don't have to pay.

tutorHints: Correct gently and ask the learner to reformulate.
Use English for meta-language when possible at A2.
